\chapter{Communication Complexity — Rank}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.DeterministicCC.Rank
\section{Overview}

This module establishes the log-rank lower bound for deterministic communication
complexity.  Given a Boolean function $f : X \to Y \to \{0,1\}$, one forms its
real-valued $0/1$ matrix $M_f$ and shows that the deterministic communication
complexity of $f$ is at least $\lceil \log_2 \mathrm{rank}(M_f) \rceil$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Boolean function matrix]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionMatrix}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionMatrix}
\leanok
Given a Boolean function $f : X \to Y \to \mathrm{Bool}$, the matrix
$M_f \in \mathbb{R}^{X \times Y}$ is defined by $(M_f)_{x,y} = 1$ if
$f\,x\,y = \mathrm{true}$ and $(M_f)_{x,y} = 0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Rank of a Boolean function]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionRank}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionRank}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionMatrix}
The rank of a Boolean function $f : X \to Y \to \mathrm{Bool}$ is the
$\mathbb{R}$-rank of its $0/1$ matrix $M_f$, i.e.\
$\mathrm{rank}(f) = \mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{R}}(M_f) \in \mathbb{N}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Rectangle indicator matrix]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.rectMatrix}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.rectMatrix}
\leanok
For a subset $R \subseteq X \times Y$, the matrix $M_R \in \mathbb{R}^{X \times Y}$
is defined by $(M_R)_{x,y} = 1$ if $(x,y) \in R$ and $(M_R)_{x,y} = 0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Rectangle matrix has rank at most one]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.rank_rectMatrix_le_one}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.rank_rectMatrix_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.rectMatrix, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle}
\difficulty{4}
If $R \subseteq X \times Y$ is a combinatorial rectangle, i.e.\ $R = A \times B$
for some $A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$, then $\mathrm{rank}(M_R) \le 1$.
This follows because $M_R$ is an outer product of the indicator vectors of $A$ and $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rank is subadditive for two matrices]
\lean{Matrix.rank_add_le}
\label{Matrix.rank_add_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For any two matrices $A, B \in \mathbb{R}^{X \times Y}$,
\[
  \mathrm{rank}(A + B) \le \mathrm{rank}(A) + \mathrm{rank}(B).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rank is subadditive over finite sums]
\lean{Matrix.rank_sum_le}
\label{Matrix.rank_sum_le}
\leanok
\uses{Matrix.rank_add_le}
\difficulty{4}
For any finite index set $\iota$, a finite set $s \subseteq \iota$, and a family
of matrices $A : \iota \to \mathbb{R}^{X \times Y}$,
\[
  \mathrm{rank}\!\left(\sum_{i \in s} A_i\right) \le \sum_{i \in s} \mathrm{rank}(A_i).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rank bounded by partition size]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionRank_le_ncard}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionRank_le_ncard}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionMatrix, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionRank, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.rank_rectMatrix_le_one, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.rectMatrix, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_part_unique, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_point_mem, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_values_eq, Matrix.rank_sum_le}
\difficulty{6}
If $\mathcal{P}$ is a monochromatic rectangle partition of a Boolean function
$f : X \to Y \to \mathrm{Bool}$, then
$\mathrm{rank}(f) \le |\mathcal{P}|$.
The proof decomposes $M_f$ as a sum of the indicator matrices of the
$1$-coloured rectangles in $\mathcal{P}$ and applies subadditivity of rank together
with the fact that each such rectangle matrix has rank at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rank bounded by $2^n$ when complexity is at most $n$]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionRank_le_pow_of_communicationComplexity_le}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionRank_le_pow_of_communicationComplexity_le}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionRank, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionRank_le_ncard, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.mono_partition_of_communicationComplexity_le}
\difficulty{3}
If the deterministic communication complexity of $f : X \to Y \to \mathrm{Bool}$
is at most $n \in \mathbb{N}$, then $\mathrm{rank}(f) \le 2^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Log-rank lower bound]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.clog_boolFunctionRank_le_communicationComplexity}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.clog_boolFunctionRank_le_communicationComplexity}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionRank, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Rank.boolFunctionRank_le_pow_of_communicationComplexity_le, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity}
\difficulty{4}
For any Boolean function $f : X \to Y \to \mathrm{Bool}$ (with $X$ finite and $Y$
a \texttt{Fintype}),
\[
  \lceil \log_2 \mathrm{rank}(f) \rceil \;\le\;
  \mathrm{DC}(f),
\]
where $\mathrm{DC}(f)$ is the deterministic communication complexity of $f$,
taken as an element of $\mathbb{N}_\infty$.
\end{theorem}
